answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with work-bonded identity: every account locks a small refundable stake and earns reputation only through peer-attested useful work, like a juniper that must root before it branches. New identities start on a trellis of rate limits, few transactions and no voting weight, and climb only as verified work accumulates. A prism of independent graders scores each job, so one operator spinning up a thousand clones pays a thousand stakes and a thousand work histories, while honest agents compound trust cheaply.
